subject: mirt d vs. b location parameters

messages.author: 5ddfe566330663b8
messages.subject: mirt d vs. b location parameters
parts:
I'm sorry if this question was previously asked and answered.

I am working with a graded response model.  Depending on which code I use (see below) the output provides "d" estimates or "b" estimates which are not identical.

model1 <- mirt(dat [ , 1:8], itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE).  
The above produces the slope (a) parameter and two d location parameters, with confidence intervals for all.

vs.

model1 <- (mirt(dat, 1, verbose = FALSE, itemtype = "graded", SE = TRUE)

IRT_parms <- coef(model1, IRTparms = TRUE, simplify = TRUE)

IRT_parms$items

The above produces b estimates which are identical to when I use the ltm package.  

So, my questions are as follows:  what are the d estimates, and how are they used?  Second, the printout of d estimates was accompanied by confidence intervals, which is very helpful.  How do I obtain either confidence intervals or standard errors of b estimates?  Is the delta method the only way to do so?  If that is the case, can someone provide a clear, step-by-step example of how to use the delta method?  I'm still relatively new to R.  

Thanks so much,

Robert
